messages:
Clara: dropping a small CX thread about confirmation language for rollbacks and canary promotes. trying to reduce user anxiety without adding too much friction. Figma: figma.com/...
Devon: interesting. are we talking microcopy in the modal only, or also the toast/undo flows?
Clara: both. modal should explain impact briefly (one line) + a short reason field optional. toast should be reassuring: e.g., "Rollback applied. Undo available for 12 seconds. Op id: abc123. View details."
Aisha: accessibility: modal must trap focus, have aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. For SR users, include the operation id in the details panel (so they can reference in audits). Also avoid long paragraphs in modal 1 keep sentences short.
Yun: copy nuance: avoid scary verbs like "destroy" or "revert" alone. Prefer verbs with explicit objects: "Revert deployment to snapshot v3.2". For confirmation input, if typed-confirm is required, keep the token short and locale-agnostic (e.g., "Type REVERT").
Tom: Ops asks we surface consequences in numbers when possible: "This will route ~45k requests/day away from v3.2". If we can't compute, say "traffic percentage change: 30%". That helps decision making.
Devon: UX friction: typed-confirm for all rollbacks is heavy. Proposal: typed-confirm only for prod namespaces or when revert affects > X% of traffic. Non-prod modal + undo toast.
Clara: agree. We'll add a policy badge in modal header when typed-confirm is required: small label "Policy: typed-confirm required" with tooltip explaining why.
Aisha: motion & contrast: modal CTA should have clear visual affordance and 4.5:1 contrast. For the toast ensure it doesn't auto-dismiss invisibly for SR users; in addition to aria-live, provide an accessible action list in the details flyout that lists recent ops with undo buttons while window valid.
Yun: mobile: use full-screen modal sheet. Keep typed-confirm input visible above keyboard and ensure keyboardDone triggers don't submit unexpectedly.
Tom: telemetry: emit event properties: op_id, user_id, namespace, affected_percent, undo_available_seconds, and policy_trigger (typed-confirm true/false). Important for postmortems.
Devon: microcopy suggestion: modal heading = "Confirm rollback"; body = one-line consequence + optional reason field + small policy badge; primary CTA = "Revert to snapshot"; secondary = "Cancel". Toast = "Rollback applied. Undo available for 12 seconds. View details."
Clara: small experiment idea: add an empathy line in modal for new users: "Need help? See docs or ping #oncall" but keep it collapsible so power users aren't slowed.
Aisha: screenreader flow: when modal opens, announce heading then a short summary. If typed-confirm required, announce instructions and place focus in input. After action completes, announce "Rollback applied. Undo available for 12 seconds" via aria-live polite.
designbot: Design review requested by Clara for `rollback-affirmation-copy`. Reviewers: Devon, Aisha, Yun, Tom. Deadline: 3 business days. :calendar:
Clara: thanks all 1 I'll update Figma frames with the modal variants (prod vs non-prod), add ARIA snippets, and a short experiment plan for the empathy line. Ping when you review the frames.
